## Overview

**Aegon, The Rogue Paragon** — a human paladin of **Aurelius**, god of wisdom and justice. Formally condemned as a traitor by the Order of the Scales, he invoked the sacred Trial by Combat and won against five champions, proving his innocence by his faith's own law. He now leads a fledgling rebel chapter — the **Order of the Protectors** — dedicated to the original oath and opposing the corruption that has consumed the Scales' High Council.

A paradox: faithful yet rebellious, honoured yet hunted, a man called Paragon who carries no proof of his title and whose actions have already contradicted the oath he swore.

---

## Appearance

A tall, broad-shouldered human with the build of a veteran warrior. Wears armour marked by field modifications and personal touches — signs of a man who follows his own path. His face is weathered, his eyes carry hard-won wisdom. A holy symbol of Aurelius hangs at his neck — a white shield emblazoned with the Relucent Verdict (a longsword of gleaming blade engraved over a balance of light). At his side: his warhammer.

---

## Background

### Origins
Aegon's mother died in childbirth. His father abandoned them before Aegon was born — no name, no reason. A local maester brought the infant to a chapel known to accept orphans. The priest who welcomed him was named **Paul**.

### Father Paul
Paul was a gentleman in his forties — kind, wise, intelligent, deeply religious. But he was not an ordinary priest. He could detect truth from lies, was skilled in combat, and carried himself with warrior discipline. Paul belonged to the **Order of the Protectors** — the knightly chapter of paladins who followed Aurelius, took oaths to protect the innocent, and swore to defeat evil.

Paul raised Aegon as his own son. Aegon showed remarkable talent with weapons. But more impressive were his emerging powers: healing with a touch, instinctive magic detection, and **visions** — fragments of past, present, and future that came to him in dreams. Paul recognized these signs. Aegon was a **Paragon** — a paladin with an extraordinary connection to the Weave, which the Order interprets as divine favour from Aurelius.

Paul revealed the truth to Aegon: he was not merely an orphan taken in by a kind priest. He was a Paragon, and the Order of the Protectors had been founded centuries ago by the first Paragons. Aegon was expected to one day understand his visions, lead with wisdom, and possibly guide the High Council itself.

### Training and the Oath
The Order of the Protectors trained its initiates at the **High Septon** — the central temple of Aurelius in **Drakhaven**, the old pre-invasion Human capital. For three years, Aegon studied combat, war, history, and religion, then faced a series of rigorous tests and trials.

He knelt before the statues of Aurelius, swore the oath, and chose his holy symbol: his **warhammer**.

> **Oath of the Order:** *"Do not fear your enemies. Be courageous and upright so that Aurelius may love you. Always speak the truth, even if it leads to your death. Safeguard the defenceless and stop evil in this world. This is your oath."*

### The Rogue Paragon
For years, Aegon served faithfully — completing missions, growing in power. His status as a Paragon became known. The High Council watched him with interest. Some whispered he was destined to lead. Others grew jealous — fanatics who believed drinking his blood might bring them closer to Aurelius, or traditionalists who saw his unique nature as a threat to the hierarchy.

Then came the news: Paul's chapel had been attacked. Aegon rode immediately. He found Paul on the chapel floor, covered in wounds. Aegon reached for his healing powers, but Paul stopped him. With his last strength, he whispered:

> *"Do not trust the Order... Trust your oath and your visions..."*

And Paul died.

### The Breaking Point
The investigation into Paul's death produced no answers. No culprit was named. The matter faded.

Aegon did not push — not because he was satisfied, but because Paul's dying words consumed him. He began watching the Order more closely. He questioned commands. The breaking point came when the High Council ordered him to execute an individual he knew — through research and his own visions — to be entirely innocent. The target's elimination served only the political interests of corrupt nobles connected to the Council.

True to his oath — *"Always speak the truth, even if it leads to your death... Safeguard the defenceless"* — Aegon refused.

The Council demanded submission. Aegon refused again. Formally labeled a traitor, he was subdued by superior forces, chained, and held for judgment.

### The Trial by Combat — Judgment of Five
In the great judgment hall, before the black-robed masters of the Order of the Scales and hundreds of assembled knights, the verdict seemed predetermined: guilty of high treason, death by public execution.

Before the sentence could be pronounced, Aegon invoked the sacred right of **Trial by Combat** — an ancient ritual of Aurelius's faith. The doctrine held that in the arena of blood, Aurelius would guide the blade of the just and deny strength to the liar. To refuse combat would be an admission that the Council feared divine judgment. They were forced to accept.

The Council invoked the harshest variant: the **Judgment of Five**. Aegon would fight alongside **four allies** against **five of the Order's mightiest champions** — veteran warriors loyal to the corrupt hierarchy.

When the Council demanded if any knight would stand with the traitor, four men rose from the crowd: **James, John, Henry, and Roderick** — driven by loyalty to Aegon and faith in his visions.

The battle took place on the temple's tournament field under a stormy sky. All ten combatants entered mounted on warhorses, in full plate, armed with heavy jousting lances. The initial charge was devastating — lances shattered on shields and breastplates. James took a lance through the thigh and fell with his mount. Roderick and John suffered grave wounds holding the line.

With horses incapacitated, the fight devolved into a brutal melee on foot. Aegon fixed on the senior champion of the Council and drove directly at him, breaking his guard and felling him with a crushing blow from his warhammer.

But then the two remaining champions — the strongest — turned on Aegon together, seeking vengeance for their commander. Alone, surrounded, while his brothers fought to recover from their wounds, Aegon held. He parried, dodged, channelled his resilience, and through sheer skill and determination broke them — disarming the first, striking through the second's armour.

When the blood settled: three champions lay dead, two gravely wounded. Aegon stood.

**He was declared innocent by divine will.**

### Renunciation and the Assassin
Victory did not bring peace. Knowing the Order of the Scales was rotten to its core and that the Council would never forgive the humiliation, Aegon **formally renounced his post** and withdrew, guiding his wounded companions to a quiet refuge.

Soon after, the corruption of the Scales became undeniable. Extortion, contract killings, and alliances with dark forces became routine. Knights and scholars who still believed in Aurelius's true purpose began seeking Aegon out, imploring him to act.

While Aegon deliberated, the Council acted first. An assassin crept into his refuge with a poisoned blade. But a fragmentary vision — and Aegon's honed combat instincts — warned him in time. He disarmed and subdued the killer, and under interrogation the assassin confessed: sent directly by the **High Council of the Order of the Scales** to eliminate the Rogue Paragon while he still recovered.

### The New Order of the Protectors
That moment was the turning point. Aegon understood: as long as the corrupt Council ruled, neither he nor his allies would ever be safe. He declared open rebellion.

### Note on Paragons
Aegon is called a Paragon — but Paragons are not unique. Other individuals in recorded history have been recognized as Paragons, each "confirmed" by the Order's interpretation of their abilities. The title is a belief, not a proven fact. Aegon has no way to prove he is one — the same phenomena the Order calls divine favour may simply be attunement to B's essence.

He founded a new **Order of the Protectors** — not as a sub-chapter of the Scales, but as a direct challenge. The order adopted the **white shield** as its emblem: purity and the Relucent Verdict of Aurelius.

The Protectors began as a small, dedicated core of **20 members**:

- **8 Warriors**: Veterans ready to give their lives for a just cause
- **7 Maesters and Scholars**: Men of knowledge to heal, preserve history, and guide the faith
- **5 Infiltrated Spies**: Agents operating within the Order of the Scales, reporting on the Council's movements

The **Four Blood Brothers** — James, John, Henry, and Roderick — became commanders of the warriors and counsellors of the new order.

With his warhammer raised and the title of **The Rogue Paragon** etched into history, Aegon ceased being merely a survivor and became the leader of a rebellion.

---

## The Oath of the Protectors (New Chapter)

The new Order of the Protectors follows a refined code — five sacred tenets that Aegon distilled from the original oath, his visions, and the lessons of Paul's death:

### 1. The Shield of the Innocents (Protect Life, Not Dogma)
> *"No blade, spell, or order shall prevail over the life of an innocent. To protect the defenceless is your first and highest duty."*

The unforgivable sin: ignoring the suffering of one unable to defend themselves, even if it jeopardizes the mission or contradicts superior orders.

### 2. The Blade of Truth (Confront Deceit and Corruption)
> *"Truth is the light that blinds the unjust. You shall never utter a lie out of cowardice, nor allow corruption to hide under sacred mantles."*

The unforgivable sin: lying for personal gain, concealing the crimes of allies, or turning a blind eye to corruption within one's own ranks.

### 3. Redeemed Trust (Destiny Lies in People, Not the Heavens)
> *"You honour the blood shed at your side. The loyalty of your brothers and sisters in arms is the only temple that cannot be destroyed."*

The unforgivable sin: betraying an ally, abandoning them in battle, or refusing to trust a companion who has proven their loyalty.

### 4. The Active Will (Change the Future, Do Not Accept It)
> *"Your visions are warnings, not chains. Fate is not written in stone — it is carved by your own will."*

The unforgivable sin: becoming paralyzed by fear of a vision, or accepting a prophesied tragedy as an inevitable decree.

### 5. The Shared Light (Break the Isolation of the Sacred)
> *"The burden of truth must not be carried in solitude. No vision, warning, or secret of fate shall be hidden from those who bleed at your side."*

The unforgivable sin: keeping vital secrets from companions — especially visions that involve their future — under the pretext of "protecting" them or assuming only you understand the divine plan.

### The Oath Contradiction
Aegon swore the original oath — *"Always speak the truth, even if it leads to your death"* — and now leads an order built on this principle. Yet he has already hidden and lied to party members. He has not told the full truth about Paul's dying words, about his visions, or about why the Scales truly condemned him. This contradiction is the central dramatic tension of his character: a man who commands truth while living a lie. It must surface during gameplay, and when it does, it will force Aegon to choose between his oath and his safety.

## Abilities
- **Paladin's Power:** Divine smite, lay on hands, aura of protection — channelled through his oath to Aurelius
- **Paragon's Blessing:** Unusually strong connection to the Weave, interpreted by the Order as divine favour
- **Visions:** Dreams of past, present, and future — initially from Aurelius, now shifting toward B's consciousness. Unreliable as tactical tools; cryptic, fragmented, open to interpretation.
- **Exceptional Combatant:** Master of warhammers, swords, spears, and axes
- **Independent Will:** Resistant to coercion, manipulation, and blind obedience

---

## Goals
1. Understand why Paul warned him against the Order — what did his dying words mean?
2. Understand why his visions are changing and where they truly come from
3. Uphold his oath — protect the innocent, defeat evil — even if it means defying the Order
4. Protect his fledgling Order of the Protectors and its scattered members
5. Expose the corruption of the Order of the Scales' High Council

---

## Relationships
- **Paul (deceased)** — Father figure, mentor. Aegon has not investigated Paul's death — consumed by the question of *why* Paul warned him.
- **The Order of the Scales** — Enemy. They framed Paul's killers, ordered Aegon's execution, and sent an assassin after him.
- **The Order of the Protectors (new)** — His creation. 20 scattered members, fragile, growing. Not yet a safe haven.
- **The Four Blood Brothers** — James, John, Henry, Roderick. Fought beside him in the trial. Now his commanders. Separated from Aegon on different missions as the rebellion spreads.
- **Aurelius** — The god he swore his oath to. Remains faithful, but shifting visions raise questions. Does Aurelius know what the Scales do in his name?
- **The Crimson Covenant** — Organization Aegon knows little about. Official story blames them for Paul's death — a story Aegon no longer trusts.

2. [?] **What exactly did Paul know?** His dying words suggest he discovered something about the Order and Aurelius himself.
3. [?] **Who attacked Paul's chapel?** Investigation produced no results. (GM note: evidence planted by Order frames the Crimson Covenant.)
